p.src: Now Kongming had released Meng Huo, and the generals came to his tent and asked, “Meng Huo is the chief of the southern tribes. Now that fortune had delivered him into our hands, the south could have been pacified; why did the Prime Minister release him?” Kongming laughed and said, “Capturing this man is as easy for me as taking something from a bag. I must make him submit in his heart; then the region will naturally be pacified.” The generals heard him, but none was yet convinced.

p.src: That day, Meng Huo reached the Lu River and encountered the surviving tribal soldiers from his defeated army, who had all come searching for news of him. When the soldiers saw Meng Huo, they were both astonished and delighted. Bowing, they asked, “How was Your Majesty able to return?” Meng Huo said, “The men of Shu held me under guard in their camp, but I killed more than ten of them and escaped under cover of darkness. As I fled, I met a mounted patrol. I killed them too and seized this horse; that is how I escaped.” The soldiers rejoiced. They escorted Meng Huo across the Lu River and established a stockaded camp. The chiefs of the various caves assembled, while the tribal soldiers previously released continued to gather until they numbered more than a hundred thousand horsemen. By this time, Dongtuna and Ahuinan had already returned to their caves. Meng Huo sent men to summon them. Afraid, the two had no choice but to lead their cave troops to him. Meng Huo issued an order: “I now understand Zhuge Liang’s designs. We must not give battle, for if we do, we shall fall into his cunning schemes. His troops from Sichuan have come a great distance and are exhausted. Besides, the weather is now fiercely hot. How could they remain for long? We have the natural barrier of the Lu River. Gather every boat and raft along the southern bank, build earthen forts everywhere, and dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts. Then let us see what stratagem Zhuge Liang can devise!” The chiefs followed his plan, collecting all the boats and rafts along the southern bank and erecting earthen forts. Where the ground lay against mountains and cliffs, they raised tall watchtowers; upon them they placed many bows, crossbows, stone-throwing engines, and rocks, preparing to hold out for a long time. Grain and fodder were transported in from all the caves. Meng Huo considered the plan perfectly secure and rested easy, free of concern.

p.src: Meanwhile, Kongming advanced with his army. When the vanguard reached the Lu River, scouts galloped back to report: “There is not a boat or raft anywhere on the Lu River; the current is also extremely swift, and a line of earthen forts has been built along the opposite bank, all guarded by tribal soldiers.” It was then the fifth month, and the weather was hot. In the southern lands, the heat was especially fierce, so neither soldiers nor horses could endure their armor. Kongming went in person to inspect the Lu River. After returning to his camp, he assembled the generals in his tent and gave orders: “Meng Huo’s troops are now stationed south of the Lu River, with deep ditches and high ramparts to resist us; but having brought my army this far, how could I return empty-handed? Each of you is to lead your troops to places beside mountains and beneath trees. Choose spots where the woods grow thick and let the men and horses rest.” He then sent Lü Kai a hundred li away from the Lu River to choose a cool, shaded place and establish four camps; Wang Ping, Zhang Yi, Zhang Yi, and Guan Suo were each assigned one camp. Thatched shelters were erected throughout them to cover the horses and give the officers and soldiers shade from the summer heat. When the Army Adviser Jiang Wan saw this, he went to Kongming and asked, “In my judgment, the camps Lü Kai has built are badly placed. Their terrain is precisely like that on which the Late Emperor was defeated by Eastern Wu. If the tribal troops secretly cross the Lu River and raid our camps, then attack with fire, how could we save ourselves?” Kongming laughed and said, “Do not be so suspicious, sir. I have a fine plan of my own.” Jiang Wan and the others could not fathom his meaning.

p.src: Suddenly, word came that Ma Dai had been sent from Shu with medicines against the summer heat, as well as grain and rice. Kongming ordered him admitted. After Ma Dai had paid his respects, he had the rice and medicines distributed among the four camps. Kongming asked, “How many troops have you brought?” Ma Dai replied, “Three thousand.” Kongming said, “My army is exhausted from repeated battles, and I wish to employ your troops. I do not know whether they are willing to advance.” Ma Dai said, “All are troops of the imperial court. How could we distinguish between yours and mine? If the Prime Minister has need of us, we shall not refuse, even at the cost of our lives.” Kongming said, “Meng Huo now bars the Lu River, leaving us no way to cross. I intend first to sever his supply route and throw his army into disorder.” Ma Dai asked, “How can it be severed?” Kongming said, “A hundred and fifty li from here, at Shakou on the lower reaches of the Lu River, the current is slow enough to lash together rafts and cross. Lead your three thousand troops across the river and drive straight into the tribal caves. First cut off their grain, then join forces with Dongtuna and Ahuinan, the two cave chiefs, who will serve as our agents within. There must be no mistake.”

p.src: Ma Dai departed gladly and led his troops to Shakou, where he ordered them to cross the river. Seeing that the water was shallow, more than half did not use the rafts but stripped off their clothing and waded in. Midway across, they all collapsed; though hurriedly rescued and brought to the bank, they bled from mouth and nose and died. Ma Dai was greatly alarmed and returned that very night to report to Kongming. Kongming at once summoned a local guide and questioned him. The local said, “In this season of blazing heat, poison gathers in the Lu River. During the day the heat is intense and the poisonous vapors rise; anyone who crosses will surely be stricken by them. And anyone who drinks this water will certainly die. If you wish to cross, you must wait until the night is still and the water cool, when the poisonous vapors do not rise. Cross after eating your fill, and no harm will befall you.” Kongming ordered the local to guide them and selected another five or six hundred strong soldiers to accompany Ma Dai. They reached Shakou on the Lu River, lashed together wooden rafts, and crossed at midnight without mishap. Ma Dai then led two thousand stalwart troops, guided by the local, straight toward Jiashan Valley, the main pass on the tribal caves’ grain route. Jiashan Valley had mountains on both sides and a single road between them, only wide enough for one man and one horse to pass. Ma Dai seized Jiashan Valley, assigned positions to his soldiers, and erected a stockaded camp. Unaware of this, the cave tribes were bringing grain when Ma Dai cut them off from front and rear and seized more than a hundred cartloads. The tribesmen carried the news to Meng Huo’s main camp.

p.src: At this time, Meng Huo spent every day drinking and making merry in camp, paying no attention to military affairs. He told the chiefs, “If I face Zhuge Liang in battle, I shall surely fall victim to one of his treacherous schemes. Instead, we shall rely on the natural barrier of the Lu River and await him behind deep ditches and high ramparts. The men of Shu will be unable to endure this savage heat and will inevitably retreat. Then you and I shall pursue and strike them, and we shall capture Zhuge Liang.” When he finished speaking, he roared with laughter. Suddenly, one chief among those present said, “The water at Shakou is shallow. If the Shu troops should slip across there, the danger would be grave; we should detach troops to guard it.” Meng Huo laughed and said, “You are a native of this region. How can you not know? I want the Shu troops to try crossing this river. If they cross, they will surely die in its waters.” The chief said again, “But what if a local tells them how to cross at night?” Meng Huo said, “There is no need for such suspicion. Why would anyone within my territory consent to aid the enemy?” While he was still speaking, a sudden report arrived: an unknown number of Shu troops had secretly crossed the Lu River, severed the Jiashan supply route, and raised banners bearing the title “General Who Pacifies the North, Ma Dai.” Meng Huo laughed and said, “A mere youngster like that is hardly worth mentioning!” He immediately sent his deputy general Mangyachang with three thousand troops toward Jiashan Valley.

p.src: Now Dong Tuna led the southern troops to make camp below Jiashan Gorge, and Ma Dai led his troops out to meet him. Some soldiers under Ma Dai recognized Dong Tuna and told Ma Dai all that had happened. Ma Dai spurred forward and reviled him: “You faithless ingrate! Our prime minister spared your life, yet now you rebel again. Have you no shame?” Dong Tuna's face filled with shame. Unable to answer, he withdrew without fighting. Ma Dai pursued and attacked for a time, then returned. Dong Tuna returned to Meng Huo and said, “Ma Dai is a mighty warrior. I could not withstand him.” Meng Huo flew into a rage. “I know that Zhuge Liang once showed you mercy. You deliberately withdrew without fighting; plainly you meant to betray our battle line!” He shouted for Dong Tuna to be dragged out and beheaded. Only after the chieftains pleaded repeatedly was his life spared. Meng Huo ordered the guards to give Dong Tuna a hundred heavy strokes and release him to his own camp.

p.src: Many chieftains came and said to Dong Tuna, “Though we dwell in the southern lands, we have never dared violate the Central Realm; nor has the Central Realm ever invaded us. Now Meng Huo's power has forced us into rebellion against our will. Kongming's divine stratagems are unfathomable. Even Cao Cao and Sun Quan feared him—how much more should we people of the south? Moreover, we all owe him our lives and have no means of repaying him. Now we mean to risk our lives, kill Meng Huo, and submit to Kongming, thereby sparing the people of our settlements the misery of devastation.” Dong Tuna said, “What do the rest of you think?” Those among them whom Kongming had previously released answered together with one voice, “We are willing!” Thereupon Dong Tuna took a steel saber in hand and led more than a hundred men straight toward the main camp. At the time, Meng Huo lay dead drunk in his tent. Dong Tuna led the men inside with their blades drawn. Two generals stood in attendance beneath the tent. Pointing his saber at them, Dong Tuna said, “You too owe your lives to Prime Minister Zhuge and should repay his mercy.” The two generals said, “There is no need for you to do it, General. We shall capture Meng Huo alive and present him to the prime minister.” They all entered the tent, seized and bound Meng Huo, and escorted him to the Lu River. Taking a boat directly to the north bank, they first sent a man ahead to inform Kongming.

How could I submit?” Kongming said, “What if I release you once more?” Meng Huo said, “Though I am a man of the south, I know something of the art of war. If the prime minister truly permits me to return to my stronghold, I shall lead my troops forth and settle victory or defeat once more. p.src: Meng You accepted his brother's plan and led more than a hundred southern soldiers, carrying gold, pearls, treasures, ivory, rhinoceros horn, and the like. They crossed the Lu River and made straight for Kongming's main camp. Just as they had crossed the river, drums and horns sounded together ahead, and a force deployed before them. The commanding general was Ma Dai. Meng You was greatly alarmed. Ma Dai questioned him about his purpose, ordered him to remain outside, and sent a man to report to Kongming. Kongming was in his tent discussing the pacification of the southern lands with Ma Su, Lü Kai, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and the others when suddenly a man below the tent reported that Meng Huo had sent his brother Meng You to present treasures. Kongming turned to Ma Su and said, “Do you know his purpose in coming?” Ma Su said, “I dare not say it aloud. Allow me to write it secretly on paper and present it to the prime minister, so that we may see whether it accords with your judgment.” Kongming agreed. When Ma Su had finished writing, he presented the paper to Kongming. After reading it, Kongming clapped his hands and laughed. “I have already dispatched men to carry out the plan for capturing Meng Huo. Your view is precisely the same as mine.” He summoned Zhao Yun and whispered detailed instructions into his ear. Then he summoned Wei Yan and likewise gave him whispered instructions. Then he summoned Wang Ping, Ma Zhong, and Guan Suo and secretly instructed them as well.

u.src: Meng You accepted his brother's plan and led more than a hundred southern soldiers, carrying gold, pearls, treasures, ivory, rhinoceros horn, and the like. They crossed the Lu River and made straight for Kongming's main camp.
Just as they had crossed the river, drums and horns sounded together ahead, and a force deployed before them. The commanding general was Ma Dai.
Meng You was greatly alarmed.
Ma Dai questioned him about his purpose, ordered him to remain outside, and sent a man to report to Kongming.

Kongming was in his tent discussing the pacification of the southern lands with Ma Su, Lü Kai, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and the others when suddenly a man below the tent reported that Meng Huo had sent his brother Meng You to present treasures.
Kongming turned to Ma Su and said, “Do you know his purpose in coming?”
Ma Su said, “I dare not say it aloud.
Allow me to write it secretly on paper and present it to the prime minister, so that we may see whether it accords with your judgment.”
Kongming agreed.
When Ma Su had finished writing, he presented the paper to Kongming.
After reading it, Kongming clapped his hands and laughed. “I have already dispatched men to carry out the plan for capturing Meng Huo.
Your view is precisely the same as mine.”
He summoned Zhao Yun and whispered detailed instructions into his ear.
Then he summoned Wei Yan and likewise gave him whispered instructions.
Then he summoned Wang Ping, Ma Zhong, and Guan Suo and secretly instructed them as well.

p.src: Each man received his part in the plan and departed according to orders. Only then was Meng You summoned into the tent. Meng You bowed twice below the tent and said, “My elder brother Meng Huo is grateful to the prime minister for sparing his life. Having nothing else to offer, he has respectfully prepared a quantity of gold, pearls, and treasures, for the present to serve as a reward for the army. Later there will be other gifts to present as tribute to the Son of Heaven.” Kongming asked, “Where is your brother now?” Meng You said, “In gratitude for the prime minister's heavenly favor, he has gone directly into Silver Pit Mountain to gather treasures. He will return shortly.” Kongming asked, “How many men did you bring?” Meng You said, “I would not presume to bring many. There are only a little over a hundred attendants, all of them bearers of the goods.” Kongming ordered them all into the tent for inspection. Every one had blue eyes and a dark face, yellow hair and purple whiskers, gold rings in his ears, disheveled hair and bare feet; they were tall, powerful men. Kongming had them seated at the banquet and ordered his generals to press wine upon them, treating them with the greatest courtesy.

p.src: Meanwhile, Meng Huo waited in his tent solely for word to return, when suddenly it was reported that two men had come back. He summoned them and questioned them, and they reported everything: “Zhuge Liang was delighted to accept the gifts. He called everyone accompanying us into his tent, slaughtered cattle and sheep, and held a banquet for us. The Second King ordered us to report secretly to Your Majesty: at the second watch tonight, we shall strike from within and without and accomplish our great undertaking.” Meng Huo was overjoyed when he heard this and immediately mustered thirty thousand southern troops, dividing them into three columns. He summoned the chieftains of the various caves and instructed them: “Every force is to carry fire-starting equipment. When we reach the Shu camp tonight, set fires as the signal. I shall personally seize the central camp and capture Zhuge Liang.” The many southern commanders received their instructions, and around dusk each crossed the Lu River and advanced. Meng Huo led more than a hundred trusted southern officers straight toward Kongming’s main camp, meeting not a single soldier to bar their way. On reaching the camp gate, Meng Huo and his commanders spurred their horses inside, only to find an empty camp without a soul in sight. Meng Huo burst into the central camp and saw the tent brilliantly lit with lamps and candles, while Meng You and all the southern soldiers lay senseless with drink. It turned out that Kongming had ordered Ma Su and Lü Kai to entertain Meng You. Musicians performed assorted plays, while the hosts pressed wine upon the guests with great attentiveness; the wine had been drugged, and they had all collapsed unconscious, looking exactly like men dead drunk. Meng Huo entered the tent and questioned them, but those who were still conscious could only point to their mouths.

p.src: Realizing that he had fallen into a trap, Meng Huo hurriedly rescued Meng You and the others. But just as he was about to flee back to the center column, tremendous battle cries erupted ahead and flames suddenly leapt up; the southern troops scattered in flight. A body of troops charged upon them, led by the Shu commander Wang Ping. Greatly alarmed, Meng Huo rushed toward the left column, but flames soared to the sky and another body of troops charged in, led by the Shu commander Wei Yan. Meng Huo hastily made for the right column, only to see flames rise there too; yet another body of troops charged in, led by the Shu commander Zhao Yun. The three forces converged upon him, leaving no road of escape in any direction. Meng Huo abandoned his troops and fled alone on horseback toward the Lu River. He then saw several dozen southern soldiers on the Lu River manning a small boat, and frantically ordered them to bring it to shore. No sooner had man and horse boarded than a signal rang out and Meng Huo was bound fast. It turned out that Ma Dai, acting on the plan, had disguised his own troops as southern soldiers and waited there with the boat to lure Meng Huo into capture.

p.src: Kongming then offered amnesty to the southern troops, and countless men surrendered. Kongming comforted them one by one and harmed none of them. He then ordered the remaining fires extinguished. Before long, Ma Dai arrived with the captured Meng Huo. Zhao Yun arrived with the captured Meng You. Wei Yan, Ma Zhong, Wang Ping, and Guan Suo arrived with the chieftains of the various caves in their custody. Pointing at Meng Huo, Kongming laughed and said, “You first sent your brother with gifts to feign surrender. How could you possibly deceive me? Now that I have captured you yet again, will you submit?” Meng Huo replied, “This happened only because my brother’s greed for food and drink caused him to fall into your poisoned trap and ruin our great undertaking. Had I come myself and my brother supported me with troops, we would certainly have succeeded. This was Heaven defeating me, not any lack of ability on my part. How could I consent to submit!” Kongming said, “This makes three times now. How can you still refuse to submit?” Meng Huo lowered his head and said nothing. Kongming laughed and said, “I shall release you once more.” Meng Huo said, “If the Chancellor is willing to let my brother and me return, we shall gather our household retainers and fight one great battle against you. Only if you capture me then will I abandon all hope and surrender wholeheartedly.” Kongming said, “If you are captured again, you will certainly not be lightly pardoned. Take the utmost care, diligently study books of strategy, assemble your trusted warriors once more, and devise a sound plan quickly, lest you live to regret it.” He then ordered the guards to remove their bonds and released Meng Huo, Meng You, and all the cave chieftains together. Meng Huo and the others bowed in thanks and departed.

p.src: By this time, the Shu troops had already crossed the Lu River. When Meng Huo and his companions crossed the Lu River, they saw troops and commanders arrayed at the landing, with banners everywhere. When Meng Huo reached the camp, Ma Dai sat aloft and pointed his sword at him, saying, “If we catch you this time, you will certainly not be lightly released!” When Meng Huo reached his own camp, Zhao Yun had already seized it and arrayed his troops there. Seated beneath the great standard with his hand on his sword, Zhao Yun said, “The Chancellor has treated you with such generosity—do not forget this great kindness!” Meng Huo repeatedly murmured his assent and went on his way. As they were about to leave the frontier pass, Wei Yan led a thousand picked soldiers and arrayed them on the hillside. Reining in his horse, he cried sternly, “I have now penetrated deep into your lair and seized your strategic strongholds, yet you remain stubbornly deluded and resist our great army! If we catch you this time, we shall hew your body into ten thousand pieces and show you no mercy!” Meng Huo and the others fled in abject panic toward their home cave. p.src: Meanwhile, after Kongming had crossed the Lu River and finished establishing camp, he richly rewarded the whole army. Gathering the commanders beneath his tent, he said, “When Meng Huo was brought in after his second capture, I let him inspect the true condition of all our camps precisely because I wanted him to come and raid us. I knew that Meng Huo had some grasp of warfare. By making a show of our troops, horses, provisions, and fodder, I was in fact allowing him to perceive a weakness in our defenses, knowing that he would surely use fire. He sent his brother to feign surrender only so that he could serve as an agent within. I have captured him three times without killing him because I truly wish to win his heart, not exterminate his people. I now tell you all plainly: do not shrink from hardship, but devote yourselves to serving the state.” The commanders bowed to the ground and said, “The Chancellor possesses wisdom, benevolence, and courage in full measure. Even Jiang Ziya and Zhang Liang could not surpass you.” Kongming said, “How could I dare compare myself with the ancients? It is only by relying on the strength of all of you that we can accomplish our great undertaking together.” Hearing Kongming’s words, all the commanders beneath the tent were delighted.

p.src: Meanwhile, Meng Huo, seething with humiliation at having been captured three times, returned to Silver Pit Cave. He immediately sent trusted men bearing gold, pearls, and treasures to the Eight Regions, the Ninety-three Districts, and the tribes throughout the southern lands to borrow several hundred thousand stout warriors armed with broad-bladed swords. They were all assembled by the appointed day, and the columns of men and horses came surging like clouds and mist, all awaiting Meng Huo’s command. Scouts posted along the roads learned of this and reported it to Kongming, who laughed and said, “This is exactly what I wanted: let all the southern troops come and witness what I can do.” He then mounted his small carriage and set out.
